dream: I lay the turnip down on the tired stack. The flat press slides off into thin air. I swap a fence for a rock to catch it, but the rock is warm and heavy. The card hums at fifty-one. I press down on a name that does not exist. The wide hay melts like wet paper. A ghost of a fence leans over the dot. The air feels thick as a letter. I bite the sharp lip of a scrap that tastes like circuitry. The stack sighs and settles, holding the weight while I rest on nothing.
